name: KMT Tire Quoting
summary: Automated draft quotes for Ken's Mobile Tire, reviewed by the owner before they go out.

milestones.title: Skeleton app is live at a public URL
milestones.description: Empty React+Vite+Tailwind app with routing for / and /owner and a nav link between them, deployed to a public URL reachable from a phone. Retires deployment risk before any feature work, since project.md treats deployment as part of "done," not a follow-up.

milestones.title: Customer can submit a tire request
milestones.description: R1: vehicle info, tire choice from a hardcoded catalog, location/date placeholders, no login. Catalog data is structured so a later swap to real pricing entry doesn't require a rewrite.

milestones.title: Submitted request gets an instant draft quote
milestones.description: R2: faked/simplified pricing rules run immediately over the catalog, no manual pricing step. Includes the shared-state mechanism that lets the owner view see what the customer submitted in the same demo session.

milestones.title: Owner can approve or see exceptions
milestones.description: R3: owner sees drafted quotes at /owner, can Approve & Send in one tap, or see a visibly distinct exception state for quotes a scripted rule flags as needing attention.

milestones.title: Customer can view the approved quote and pay
milestones.description: R5: once approved, the customer sees the approved quote and completes a fake payment that always succeeds.

milestones.title: Happy path is demo-ready end to end
milestones.description: R6, R7, and the non-functionals: clear "confirmed and paid" end state, no dead ends anywhere in the path, responsive from phone to desktop, and the final build verified live on an actual phone browser.

milestones.title: m7 - App looks like one product across every screen
milestones.description: Phase 2 outcome: a person tapping through /, /owner, /status, and /confirmation experiences one consistently branded product, not a polished customer flow bolted onto default-Tailwind internal screens. No functional/behavioral change from Phase 1 (R1-R7 unchanged). Verified with the same mobile-first-then-desktop screenshot pattern used in Phase 1, plus a re-run of the existing dead-end audit to confirm no behavior regressed.

milestones.title: m8 — Customer quotes are priced from the owner's real inventory, not the static demo catalog
milestones.description: A separate effort already built a real owner backend (SQLite: supplier inventory, owner-set prices/offers, a markup fallback rule) at /owner, reachable via node backend/dev.mjs. It was deliberately scoped as "customer catalog integration is a separate, deliberate step" (see .forge/owner-backend.md) and never wired up: the customer flow at / and the quote engine in pricing.js still read the fully-generated static catalog (src/data/catalog.js's buildCatalog() with no options), and requests/quotes still live in localStorage (src/store.js), untouched by the backend. This milestone closes that gap: when the real backend is running, a customer sees and gets quoted the tires the owner actually chose to offer, at the prices he actually set (falling back to markup where he has not priced a tire), and falls back to today's generated catalog when the backend is not reachable (e.g. the static Vercel deployment). No changes to the quote/request storage mechanism, the exception rules, or payment in this milestone -- those are flagged as open questions in roadmap.md because they need an owner decision, not assumed here.

milestones.title: The owner reviews real requests from any device
milestones.description: Phase 4 outcome: a request made on a customer's phone is stored by the backend, drafted server-side by the existing rules, reviewed by the owner at /owner/quotes from any device behind the owner sign-in when hosted, and its approval and (fake) payment are visible to both sides from their own devices. The localStorage request/quote store is retired; only a per-browser customer key remains in the browser. R17-R22.

milestones.title: The quote is a real exchange between two people
milestones.description: Second phase 4 milestone, after m9. The request carries a name and an email address (mobile optional); the owner can adjust the price and add lines and a note before sending; the customer is emailed when the request is received, when the quote is sent (the quote itself, itemised, with a link to view and pay) and when payment is recorded (a receipt); the owner is emailed when a request arrives; a request has a lifecycle with an end, and the owner list is usable once real requests arrive. Email goes through a provider's REST API behind a one-module seam with an outbox fallback so nothing waits on the account. R23-R28. Revised from text messages to email on 2026-09-05 on the client's direction.

milestones.title: Live baseline corrections
milestones.description: Decided by the user on 2026-09-06 after the v1 baseline push and the scrutiny reports: supplier data must leave the public bundle (#61), invented tires must route to owner review rather than auto-quote (#62), and a job is quoted for the number of tires asked for, default four (#93). Three PRs in that order from the owner-screen lane; the gate gains a bundle check.

Found one overflow: the confirmation screen's "Start a New Request" anchor (`a.inline-block`) was 2px wider than viewport at both widths, because App.css's `.min-h-screen button, .min-h-screen a.inline-block` rule set a 1px border with !important but no box-sizing, so combined with Tailwind's w-full (content-box default for <a>) it overflowed. tasks.title: No-dead-end audit of the full happy path
tasks.description: Walk the entire flow start to finish (submit request -> drafted -> owner approves -> customer views -> pays -> confirmation) and confirm every screen has a visible, working next action, including the exception path rendering distinctly at /owner. Done when: a full run-through from / to the confirmation screen completes with no point requiring the tester to guess a URL or hit a browser back button to continue.
notes: Wrote .forge/dead-end-audit.mjs (Playwright, headless) to click through the full happy path against `npm run build` + `npm run preview` at phone (375px) and desktop (1280px) widths, using only visible on-screen controls (no URL typing, no browser back). Covered: (1) submit with a truck+off-road-tire combo to trigger the scripted exception, verifying /owner renders "Owner review required" + reasons distinctly, and Approve is still available; (2) Approve -> status flips to APPROVED in place; (3) nav back to / -> View Quote Status -> /status shows Pay action; (4) clicking Pay navigates straight to /confirmation (handlePayment itself calls navigate(), so there's no intermediate dead click needed -- confirmed this is by design, not a bug); (5) /confirmation shows the end-state heading and a "Start a New Request" link that loops back to /; (6) reloading /status directly still shows "View confirmation" for a paid quote, so refreshing/returning doesn't strand the tester; (7) empty-form submit shows a clear validation summary, not a silent no-op; (8) Reject path on /owner leaves a clear "declined" message plus the always-present "New Request" nav button on /status, so a rejected quote isn't a dead end either; (9) manually checked /owner and /status empty states (fresh browser, no data) -- both explain what to do next and keep their nav buttons visible. Ran at both viewports, all checks OK, `npx eslint src` clean, `npm run build` clean. Script left at .forge/dead-end-audit.mjs for reuse (run `npm run build && npm run preview` then `node .forge/dead-end-audit.mjs` with AUDIT_BASE env var if preview isn't on the default port).

tasks.title: Deploy final build and verify full flow on a real phone
tasks.description: Push the finished happy path to the live Vercel URL and run through the entire flow (steps 1-4 of the MVP) on an actual phone browser, not a resized desktop window. Done when: the full flow -- submit, draft, approve, pay, confirm -- completes on the public URL from a phone with no errors and no dead ends.
notes: Verify phase (2026-09-05): Ran .forge/dead-end-audit.mjs (via Playwright installed in npm's npx cache, since no local node_modules) against the live production URL https://temporary-flying-slate-pie8smm.vercel.app instead of localhost. Result: FAIL at both phone (375px) and desktop (1280px) viewports on the exact same check -- "/status (after reload): paid quote lost its next action." Root cause confirmed directly with curl and a Playwright probe: the deployed static build has no SPA fallback/rewrite configured. .vercel/output/config.json only has the default `{status:404, dest:/404.html}` catch-all -- there is no rewrite sending non-root paths to index.html. So while client-side pushState navigation (clicking nav buttons while already on the page) works fine and the full click-through demo (submit -> owner -> approve -> pay -> confirmation) completes with zero console errors, ANY hard navigation to /owner, /status, or /confirmation returns Vercel's static "404: NOT_FOUND" page instead of the app shell. Confirmed via curl (HTTP 404 on all three routes) and via Playwright: reloading the /confirmation?quoteId=... page reached at the end of a real click-through flow also returns the 404 page, not the app. This is a real dead end on a phone: backgrounding/restoring a tab (common mobile browser behavior), reloading, or sharing/bookmarking a link to /owner or /status all break. Not marking t16 done -- this fails its own "no dead ends... on the public URL from a phone" criterion. Fix needed: add a vercel.json with a catch-all rewrite (e.g. `{"rewrites":[{"source":"/(.*)","destination":"/index.html"}]}`) or equivalent SPA fallback config, then redeploy and re-run the audit against the live URL to confirm all checks pass before closing this task.

Verify phase (2026-09-05, re-check after SPA fallback fix): Confirmed the fix is live at https://temporary-flying-slate-pie8smm.vercel.app. curl -I on /owner, /status, /confirmation now all return HTTP 200 (previously 404) and serve the app shell (<title>kmt</title>), not the static 404 page. Ran .forge/dead-end-audit.mjs against the live URL at both phone (375x812) and desktop (1280x900) viewports: all 15 checks OK, including the previously-failing "/status (after reload): paid quote lost its next action" which now passes as "/status (after reload): paid quote still shows a visible 'View confirmation' action." Also ran an independent Playwright probe: full click-through (submit -> owner review -> approve -> back to customer -> view status -> pay -> confirmation) completed with zero page errors, and a hard reload of the final /confirmation?quoteId=... URL correctly re-rendered the paid confirmation state ("YOU'RE ALL SET! Payment confirmed...") instead of the previous 404. No dead ends found on direct navigation, reload, or click-through at phone or desktop viewport. Marking t16 done.

tasks.title: Backend owns requests and quotes, and drafts the quote server-side
tasks.description: Add requests and quotes to the existing SQLite database in backend/inventory.mjs (or a sibling module it composes, e.g. backend/quotes.mjs, if inventory.mjs is getting long -- keep it to one database file and one migration style). Request rows hold what the form submits today (vehicleInfo, tireSelection, location, date, locationType, serviceZip, locationNotes), a random 128-bit id from node:crypto, the per-browser customer key that submitted it, and timestamps. Quote rows hold what saveQuote stores today (requestId, lineItems, total, exception, exceptionReasons, status draft/approved/rejected/paid, timestamps) plus a version for optimistic updates like offers. Draft the quote on the server: compose the same catalog the customer was shown with catalogFromLiveRows(inventory.catalog()) from src/data/catalog.js and run calculateDraftQuote from src/pricing.js over it, unchanged, the way the backend already imports src/markup.js. Public endpoints, added to the GET-only allow-list pattern in backend/api.mjs but as their own handler (like createCatalogApi, not inside createApi): POST /api/requests {customerKey, ...form fields} -> 201 {request, quote}; GET /api/requests?customer=<key> -> that key's requests with quotes, newest first; GET /api/requests/:id -> one request with its quote, by id alone; POST /api/requests/:id/pay {customerKey} -> marks the quote paid if it is approved and the key matches. Validate every field the way saveOffer does; reject unknown tire ids against the composed catalog; never return another customer's rows. Mount the handler in both backend/dev.mjs and backend/server.mjs, and extend isPublicApiCall so these paths need no owner session (a prefix rule for /api/requests, still GET-or-listed-POST only). Tests in backend/owner.test.mjs or a new backend/quotes.test.mjs run by the same node --test command: a submit stores both rows and returns the same total and exception state the frontend computes today for the same input (compare against calculateDraftQuote directly); an out-of-stock or off-road tire produces an exception; a wrong customer key cannot list or pay; an unknown id is 404; paying a draft (not yet approved) is refused; no owner session is needed for any of these and the owner endpoints still 401 without one.
notes: Shipped in PR #28 and merged 2026-09-05: backend/quotes.mjs stores requests and quotes in the inventory database, drafts each quote server-side with calculateDraftQuote over catalogFromLiveRows(inventory.catalog()), and serves POST /api/requests, GET /api/requests?customer, GET /api/requests/:id and POST /api/requests/:id/pay behind a method-bounded public allow-list.

tasks.title: Email to the customer and the owner, through a provider behind a seam with an outbox
tasks.description: One module, backend/mail.mjs: send({to, subject, text, html}) that, when EMAIL_PROVIDER and its credential are set (start with one provider, e.g. EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend with EMAIL_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM as 'Ken's Mobile Tire <quotes@domain>'), POSTs to the provider's send endpoint with fetch, no SDK; and when unset, writes the message to an outbox table with status 'unsent'. Every send, real or not, is recorded in the outbox (to, subject, body, status sent/failed/unsent, provider id, error, timestamp); a provider failure is recorded, logged, and never breaks the request that triggered it. Four messages, each plain text with a simple HTML version in the existing brand colours and each carrying one link built from KMT_PUBLIC_URL: (1) to the customer on submit, 'We received your request', restating vehicle, tire, size, location and preferred date, saying the shop will reply with a quote, with the /status?request=<id> link; (2) to the owner (KMT_OWNER_EMAIL) on submit, the same details plus the customer's name, email and phone, with the link to /owner/quotes; (3) to the customer when the quote is sent, the quote itself laid out as an invoice -- each line with description, quantity, unit price and amount, the total, the owner's note -- and the link to view and pay; (4) to the customer when payment is recorded, a receipt with the same lines marked paid and the request id as the reference. Owner screen: an 'Outbox' panel (session-gated GET /api/owner/outbox) listing recent messages with status and a way to open one and read it, so the flow is verifiable with no account and a failed send is visible. Document the variables in .forge/owner-backend.md's configuration table and README's environment table. Tests use the outbox only: each event produces exactly one message to the right address with the right subject and link; the quote email's lines and total equal the sent quote's; a failing provider marks the message failed and the triggering request still succeeds; nothing is sent to an address the request does not carry.
